findings.problem: Hydrogenation is listed only for alkenes (COR 2.8); adding H₂ to an alkyne is not in the outline, though it follows from alkene hydrogenation.
Saying 6 is double the number of ester bonds tells the student the key is half of 6.
findings.new_text: 6 uses two hydroxides for each ester bond. Each ester bond uses just one hydroxide, so count the ester bonds again.

findings.problem: 'one more C=C is elsewhere' gives the total directly (2 + 1).
findings.new_text: 2 mol counts the double bonds in only one chain. Check every chain for C=C bonds.

findings.problem: Stating that one chain has two C=C and another has one gives the total directly.
findings.new_text: 1 mol counts only one C=C. Look at each of the three chains, since more than one of them may have C=C bonds.

findings.problem: The explanation names chains by position (top, bottom, drawn to the left), which depends on how the SMILES is rendered and may not match the picture.
findings.replace: The top chain has 1 C=C, the bottom chain has 2 and the chain on the middle carbon of glycerol (drawn to the left) is saturated
findings.with: One end chain has 1 C=C, the other end chain has 2 and the chain on the middle carbon of glycerol is saturated

findings.problem: Telling the student each molecule has three C=C leaves only the scaling step.
findings.new_text: 2.0 mol H₂ gives only one H₂ per molecule. Count the C=C bonds in each chain, and remember that adding H₂ changes how the chains pack.

findings.problem: Food energy values in kcal per gram are CHEM 3A (energy and nutrition) content; the 3B outline treats metabolic energy only as ATP yields.
The stem asks about Calories but the table gives kcal; a student new to US food labels may not know a Calorie is a kcal.
findings.replace: what percent of its Calories come from fat
findings.with: what percent of its Calories (kcal) come from fat

findings.problem: Food energy values in kcal per gram are CHEM 3A (energy and nutrition) content; the 3B outline treats metabolic energy only as ATP yields.
'The cycle count is also one too many' gives the keyed cycle count.
findings.new_text: Each acetyl CoA carries 2 carbons, so 14 acetyl CoA would need 28 carbons. Also think about how the last cycle changes the number of cycles.

findings.problem: Food energy values in kcal per gram are CHEM 3A (energy and nutrition) content; the 3B outline treats metabolic energy only as ATP yields.
The hint lists every count (2 ATP, 10 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 GTP), leaving only multiplication for a difficulty-3 tally question.
findings.new_text: Tally the ATP, NADH, FADH₂ and GTP from each stage for one glucose. Remember that one glucose gives two pyruvate and two turns of the citric acid cycle.
